thread.title: Apple Should Buy Netflix or These 2 Other Companies, JPMorgan Says

title: Apple Should Buy Netflix or These 2 Other Companies, JPMorgan Says
text:
Apple Should Buy Netflix or These 2 Other Companies, JPMorgan Says By Feb. 4, 2019 9:47 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Zhang Kaiyv Text size
The market is buzzing on which companies Apple (ticker: AAPL) should buy with its massive cash war chest. Netflix continued to gain subscribers, but reported lower profit in the fourth quarter as it spends more to fend off new competition from Disney, NBC WarnerMedia and others. WSJ’s Jason Bellini explains.
JPMorgan ’s Apple analyst Samik Chatterjee believes Apple should look in the video streaming content, videogaming, and smart home speaker markets for its next big deal. He has targeted Netflix , Activision Blizzard , and Sonos as good fits for the tech giant.
CEO Tim Cook reminded investors in a letter last month that Apple’s goal is to be “net-cash neutral” over time, meaning that Apple needs a use for its $130 billion in net cash. He also made it clear the company continues to ponder large acquisitions as well in a recent interview.
Investors “hope the firm uses its balance sheet strength to insulate the business against often-seen disruptions in the technology landscape, some of which Apple itself has driven in the past,” the analyst wrote on Monday. “We find three industries to be of the most strategic value, providing potential growth opportunities to leverage services over a wider installed base.”
Apple stock was up 0.6% in Monday’s premarket session to $167.45. Chatterjee reiterated his Overweight rating and $228 price target for the shares.
For the video streaming market, Netflix (NFLX) is the obvious fit for Apple because of its lead in original content and established scale, according to the analyst. He noted Netflix already has more than 139 million paid subscribers world-wide.
Netflix declined to comment.
In this recent episode of The Readback, Alex Eule is joined by Barron’s tech reporter Tae Kim to talk about how Apple lost its way and where it goes from here. You can sign up for the podcast in iTunes or wherever you listen to podcasts .
In the videogaming market, Chatterjee said Activision Blizzard (ATVI) is the best strategic fit for Apple because of its leading content that can be used on a variety of platforms including consoles, PCs, and smartphones.
(Last month, Barron’s suggested Apple should buy Nintendo , so the smartphone maker can get more exposure to the large and growing gaming industry, while benefiting from a vast array of potential revenue synergies.) Newsletter Sign-up
Chatterjee believes Sonos (SONO) is the best target in the smart home speaker market because of its high-end competitive position and the upper-income demographic of its customer base.
Apple, Activision Blizzard, and Sonos didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
Chatterjee said the recent selloff in the stock market and technology sector is giving Apple an opportunity to buy companies at lower prices.
“We believe valuations for technology companies are more digestible currently relative to mid-2018 and would argue that it is an opportune time for Apple to leverage its strong balance sheet to further consolidate its ecosystem,” he wrote.
